result:
I reviewed the diff against `SUPERBOSS_DISPATCH_PROMPT.md`'s tiered-trust rules and wrote `review-verdict.json` with verdict **reject** (tier2, still requires human sign-off regardless).

Key finding: the new `prompt_lifecycle` business-rule thresholds (canary duration, eval pass rate, eval budget) are resolved through the existing org-override chain in `module-rules-resolver.ts`, but `prompt_templates`/`prompt_versions`/`prompt_eval_runs` are explicitly platform-wide tables with no `orgId`. Since `setModuleRule()` only requires plain `admin` (rank 5) with no moduleKey allowlist, any org's admin can zero out the canary/eval-pass gates for their own org, letting that org's `veridian_admin` (rank 6) promote **any** platform-wide prompt template to Production while bypassing the safety gates every other tenant relies on — a real cross-tenant privilege/trust-boundary bug baked into the governance engine this phase is supposed to be hardening. The eval-budget guardrail has the same root cause (org-overridable threshold vs. globally-aggregated spend). I also flagged a related ABAC-scoping inconsistency and an overly broad PII credit-card regex as secondary issues.

Everything else (schema additivity, migration idempotency reasoning, maker-checker logic, audit wiring, permission-service structure) looked sound. No `.github/workflows/**` files are touched in this diff.
